The statement’s caution about virus-driven downside risks is balanced by a policy framework that literature suggests is supportive: the shift to average inflation targeting (as announced by Chair Powell in 2020) is consistent with inflation-forecast targeting to re-anchor expectations at 2% over time (Svensson and Woodford, 2005) and with the Taylor principle emphasized by Clarida and coauthors, while continued QE and explicit forward guidance at the zero lower bound aim to ease financial conditions and support credit intermediation in the presence of credit frictions (Curdia and Woodford, 2008). Net tone: cautiously negative on near-term outlook, but strengthened by credible commitment tools that mitigate deflation risk and bolster the recovery.
